geometry_edits.rationale: Convert the split-wing into a clearer courtyard-based public threshold while keeping the compact mass ancestry intact.
Carve a more legible public void that can function as neighborhood entry space.
Align the void to the program access side so the street edge reads as open rather than sealed.
Preserve the dominant gesture while making the courtyard the visible organizing rule.

graph_edits.rationale: Replace the split-wing emphasis with a clearer carved-public threshold strategy while preserving the dominant compact mass.
Keep the primary articulation aligned to the long site direction so the mass reads as one continuous street building.
Reduce over-fragmentation so the mass maintains a dominant primary body instead of two competing pieces.
Strengthen the legible ground-level public threshold along the access edge.
Widen the ground connection to create a clearer public seam rather than a thin sliver.
Increase the void enough to read as intentional court/entry space, not accidental separation.

rationale: The candidate reads as a single object in the isometric and front views, but its massing language is not well resolved across all four views: the split-wing/tilted form changes character substantially and the top view shows a more fragmented carved figure than the elevations suggest. The dominant gesture is present, but hierarchy is muddled by the aggressive BOOK mutation and the open-space figure is weakly legible as public space rather than incidental subtraction. Most importantly, the visible ground response to the verified access edge is not convincing: the blue frontage is met by a largely sealed or semantically indirect mass, with no strong court, seam, undercut, or entry void that clearly addresses the access side. Program-wise, neighborhood living needs an active threshold and a coherent public/collective void; this form trends toward an abstract sculpted object or stepped wedge more than a compact street building. The reference set supports either a simple active-edge pavilion strategy or a clearer courtyard/terrace relationship, but the candidate currently does not deliver either strongly enough for hard pass.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Much more pavilion-like and rectilinear than the candidate; it demonstrates active edge clarity, not the candidate’s steep split-wing section.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Simple street-facing low-rise mass with a clear public threshold and an attached vertical/service element; the mass reads as one compact occupiable object rather than a composition of fragments.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Counterfactual is a much larger housing slab and waterfront condition; transfer the sectional logic, not the overall scale or dramatic slope.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Terraced/courtyard massing can support neighborhood living when the void is legible and the upper mass remains subordinate to a coherent ground rule.

warnings: Visible access-edge response is weak relative to the blue frontage.
The form is only partially coherent across views; the top view suggests internal fragmentation and possible overlapping subvolumes.
The silhouette is more sculptural/steeply clipped than capacity-bearing or program-legible.
Do not reward box-filling; the parcel is occupied but not convincingly answered by a public threshold.
